latin.481: ANNOTATIO IV. De Vera circa Eucharistiam S. Sententia, per omnia æræ Christianæ secula ad hunc usque diem, edocta. ad pag. 37.
latin.482: §. I. Tandem Historiæ de vera Sententia Eucharistica per compendium condendæ, accingimur, cujus ut primordium, ita fundamentum in ipsis Institutionis S. Cœnæ verbis & collocandum arbitramur, & à Christo ipso collocatum advertimus, dicente, Hoc est corpus meum, Hic est sanguis meus.
latin.483: Hæc enim verba Christi de pane ab eo accepto, benedicto, fracto, sicque discipulis suis dando, de calice item benedicto similiter, discipulisque porrigendo, enunciata, etsi ob expositas Annotatione Ima rationes, quatenus propositionem plenam ac integram absolvunt, Tropum includant eòque propositiones figuratæ dicendæ sint, non inficiatis omnino vel ipsis Lutheranis, quin paucioribus quidem explicitè, implicitè omnibus idem ipsum admittere necesse habentibus, tamen talem tropum minimè omnium continere eòque sensu figuratas constituere propositiones à quoquam Orthodoxorum, Lutheranorum pariter ac Reformatorum perhibebuntur, quæ corpus & sanguinem Christi Cœnâ S. eliminant.
latin.484: At verò Corpus & Sanguinem Christi, verè ac realiter, propriè & citra omnem figuram, in S. Eucharistia, & præsentia esse, & ab omnibus, juxta Institutionem Christi S. Cœnâ utentibus, participari, veræ, genuinæ & orthodoxæ de S. Cœna sententiæ animam expedit.
latin.485: Unde rectissimè Reverendissimus Cosinus Historiam suam Transsubstantiationis papalis, his verbis auspicatur: Quæ à Christo Domino, in solenni hujus augustissimi sacramenti Institutione, ad perpetuam sui memoriationem, prolata sunt verba, nempe, Hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis traditur, Hic est sanguis meus qui pro vobis effunditur, omnino infallibilia atque verissima esse, universa per orbem terrarum sancta confitetur Ecclesia. Si quis autem contrarium affirmaverit, aut veracitatem Christi in dubium vocare ausus fuerit, dictisve ejus fidem derogaverit, nec iis assensum suum præbuerit, nisi per figmentum & nudam figuram expositis & detortis, illum in Ecclesiis nostris nec tolerare, nec excusare vel possumus, vel debemus.
latin.486: Quicquid enim sacrosancta docet Scriptura, id nobis verum ac indubitatum esse oportet. Verum igitur nec minùs indubium esse fatendum est, quod dixit Christus: Caro mea verè est cibus & sanguis meus est potus; quæ juxta B. Paulum per panem & poculum nobis communicantur: eundem enim panem communionem corporis Christi, itidemque poculum, sanguinis ipsius poculum, appellavit.

pass_a.481: ANNOTATIO IV. On the True Sentence concerning the Sacred Eucharist, taught through all the ages of the Christian era down to this very day. to p. 37.
pass_a.482: §. I. At last we gird ourselves to composing in brief the History of the true Eucharistic Sentence, whose beginning as well as foundation we judge is to be placed in the very words of the Institution of the Sacred Supper, and we observe placed there by Christ Himself, saying, This is my body, This is my blood.
pass_a.483: For these words of Christ, uttered concerning the bread taken by Him, blessed, broken, and so given to His disciples, and likewise concerning the cup blessed and offered to the disciples, although on account of the reasons set out in Annotatio I, insofar as they complete a full and entire proposition, they include a Trope and therefore are to be called figurative propositions — the Lutherans themselves by no means wholly denying it, indeed a few explicitly, and all implicitly having to admit the same — yet such a trope as would constitute figurative propositions in that sense which eliminates Christ’s body and blood from the Sacred Supper will be alleged by no Orthodox, Lutherans and Reformed alike.
pass_a.484: But that the Body and Blood of Christ are truly and really, properly and apart from every figure, present in the Sacred Eucharist, and are participated in by all who use the Sacred Supper according to Christ’s Institution, is the soul of the true, genuine, and orthodox sentence concerning the Sacred Supper.
pass_a.485: Whence most rightly the Most Reverend Cosinus opens his History of papal Transsubstantiation with these words: The words brought forth by Christ the Lord in the solemn Institution of this most august sacrament for the perpetual memorial of Himself, namely, This is my body, which is given for you, This is my blood which is poured out for you, the whole holy Church throughout the world confesses to be altogether infallible and most true. But if anyone shall have affirmed the contrary, or dared to call Christ’s truthfulness into doubt, or derogated faith from His sayings, and not given his assent to them unless they are explained and twisted by a fiction and bare figure, him we neither can nor ought to tolerate or excuse in our Churches.
pass_a.486: For whatever Holy Scripture teaches, that ought to be true and undoubted for us. Therefore it must be confessed true and no less undoubted what Christ said: My flesh is truly food and my blood is drink; which according to blessed Paul are communicated to us through bread and cup: for he called the same bread the communion of Christ’s body, and likewise the cup the cup of His blood.

481: ANNOTATIO IV opens: On the True Sentence concerning the Sacred Eucharist.
It is the sentence taught through every age of the Christian era down to this day (Autor p. 37).
482: §.I: we now briefly write the history of that true Eucharistic sentence.
Its beginning and foundation sit in the Institution words themselves — This is my body, This is my blood — placed there by Christ.
483: Those words (bread taken, blessed, broken, given; cup blessed and offered) do include a trope as full propositions — Annotatio I’s reasons; even Lutherans must admit it, a few explicitly, all implicitly.
But no Orthodox — Lutheran or Reformed — will say the trope is the kind that eliminates Christ’s body and blood from the Sacred Supper.
484: The soul of the true, genuine, orthodox Supper sentence is this:
Christ’s Body and Blood are truly and really present in the Eucharist — properly, not by bare figure — and are participated in by all who use the Supper per Christ’s Institution.
485: Cosinus (Most Reverend) rightly opens his History of papal Transsubstantiation with the Institution words: This is my body given for you; This is my blood poured out for you — the whole Church confesses them infallible and most true.
Anyone who twists them into a fiction and bare figure, denying Christ’s truthfulness, we neither can nor ought to tolerate or excuse in our churches.
486: Whatever Holy Scripture teaches must be true and undoubted for us — so also Christ’s My flesh is truly food and my blood drink, communicated through bread and cup per Paul.
Paul called the bread the communion of Christ’s body and the cup the cup of His blood.
Stop before §.II (John 6 and Paul as the mode-commentaries on Institution).
